title: What Makes Us a Family? 57th IFFI Closing Film Explores the Meaning of Belonging
subtitle: Actors of ‘We Are All Strangers’ reflect on growing up, taking responsibility and finding human connections
body_text:
Posted On: 28 NOV 2026 3:48PM by PIB Mumbai Release ID: 2343028 Views: 65 A A Print Share X Facebook Instagram WhatsApp Copy Article Link
Read in: English
Goa, 28 November 2026 What makes a family — shared blood, a common home or the bonds that people gradually build with one another? This question lies at the heart of We Are All Strangers , the closing film of the 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI). Directed by Anthony Chen, the 157-minute feature in Mandarin and English explores family relationships, the uncertainties of adulthood and the meaning of belonging. Singaporean actors Koh Jia Ler and Regene Lim reflected on these themes at a press conference organised by the Press Information Bureau (PIB) in Goa today. The film completes Chen's Growing Up trilogy, following Ilo Ilo (2013) and Wet Season (2019). Set in contemporary Singapore, the film follows 21-year-old Junyang and his father, Boon Kiat, as new relationships and unexpected responsibilities reshape their lives. As four individuals come to share a home, the story explores family relationships, the uncertainties of adulthood and the bonds that gradually develop between people who initially struggle to understand one another. Reflecting on his journey with the Growing Up trilogy, Koh said he had grown as an actor alongside the films. Recalling his selection from around 8,000 children, he said he had no formal acting training when he began working with Chen. What started as an enjoyable experience during school holidays gradually evolved into a deeper engagement with cinema and performance through his subsequent collaborations with the director. Speaking about his character Junyang, Koh observed that he is compelled to take on family responsibilities while simultaneously trying to find his place in society. He noted that some of his personal experiences had also found their way into the film. The challenges of entering adulthood, making difficult choices and finding direction, he said, were experiences that young audiences across the world could relate to. Explaining the significance of the film's title, Lim, who plays Lydia, said that even people connected by blood, such as the father and son in the story, can remain strangers to one another. As four individuals begin living under one roof, they gradually learn to understand and accept each other, discovering that family is shaped not merely by biological ties but also by understanding, acceptance and emotional connections. Lim also spoke about returning to acting after studying communications at Nanyang Technological University, which rekindled her interest in the craft. She described cinema as a medium that allows audiences to discover lives, countries and cultures different from their own. Koh expressed hope that the film would introduce international audiences to the everyday lives of people in Singapore, beyond the country's familiar image of prosperity. Through its intimate portrayal of family, responsibility and the uncertainties of growing up, We Are All Strangers offers a fitting close to IFFI 2026's theme, Stories Without Borders . Its exploration of belonging and human relationships underscores how emotions and experiences can connect people across cultures and geographies. The press conference was moderated by Shri Kiran Murali.
